concepts.why: Secular scholar / all readers: Genesis 1:9 says the waters were gathered into one place so the dry land might appear; it says nothing of a boundary, a bar or a limit, so it shares the sea but does not hold the concept (the other four each say 'boundary', 'bars and doors', 'no farther', 'cannot cross'). Drop it (or keep it only as a front-page or secondary item). The four that remain are exact on their notes.

Secular scholar / Reformed / Catholic: the name is 'Rule over the fish of the sea'. Psalm 115:16 says only that the earth is given to mankind and the highest heavens are the LORD's; it names no rule over creatures. It shares the idea of a gift of the earth, not the concept. Drop it. (James 3:7 is kept: it says the creatures of the sea have been tamed by man, which is the thing named.)

Secular scholar: the name is the work of the garden, 'to cultivate and keep it'. Psalm 104:23 says man goes out to his work and labor until evening in general (it sits in a verse about the lions' night and man's day), not tilling or keeping the ground. Psalm 104:14 already carries the crops man cultivates. Drop 104:23. Genesis 3:23 (to work the ground, after the banishment) is acceptable because it names the work of the ground; leave it unframed as a reversal or a curse.

Baptist/dispensational, Jewish and secular readers, Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed: the name is 'The seventh day'. Mark 2:27 speaks of the Sabbath being made for man and never mentions the seventh day or God's rest; Hebrews 4:9–10 speaks of a Sabbath rest that 'remains' for the people of God. Set under a concept of the seventh day of creation beside Genesis 2 and Exodus, these two make the grouping say the Old Testament Sabbath is taken up in the New Testament (the Sabbath-to-rest reading, and an Israel/church question), which the concept may not do. Neither says 'the seventh day'. Keep Genesis 2:1–3, Exodus 20:11, Exodus 31:17 and Hebrews 4:4 (which quotes Genesis 2:2 and says 'seventh day'). Mark 2:27 and Hebrews 4:9–10 belong, if anywhere, under a Sabbath theme.

concepts.name: The life of every living thing is in His hand
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Lutheran: the name 'All creatures look to You' is said only by Psalm 104:27 and the sense of Psalm 145:15; Nehemiah 9:6, Job 12:10, Job 34:14–15 and Acts 17:25 say God gives and holds life and breath, and none says the creatures look to Him. The name says more than five of the seven passages. Rename in the texts' words (Job 12:10), which also fits Psalm 104:28 and 145:16 ('You open Your hand'), Job 34:14–15, Nehemiah 9:6 and Acts 17:25. Psalm 147:8–9 is the weakest fit (God provides food and rain, no 'hand'); acceptable as an instance of the same provision, or move it if the drafter prefers. Alternatively keep the current name and drop Neh 9:6, Job 12:10, Job 34:14–15, Acts 17:25 into a second concept; but one renamed concept is simpler. All notes are exact quotations.

secondary_or_links: Links: 'Law/Wisdom' and 'Wisdom Literature' both appear; if both are real theme names they overlap (Exodus 20:11 and the wisdom passages). Confirm both exist as separate themes or keep one.

Secondary 'Be fruitful and multiply → fill the earth': Genesis 35:11 says 'Be fruitful and multiply' to Jacob but not 'fill the earth', and the next words are about a nation and kings; consider dropping 35:11 so every verse holds the phrase named by the arrow.
Secondary 'The tree of life': Genesis 3:22–24 is longer than needed; 3:22 and 3:24 carry the tree. No tradition-side concern in the grouping.

Secondary 'The whole creation has been groaning → set free from its bondage to decay' sits correctly as secondary; it does not say the Old Testament is fulfilled, and it should not be promoted to the core concept 'A new heaven and a new earth' (readers differ on its sense).

missing.why: The prophets and Psalms repeatedly say the Maker 'stretched out the heavens' and laid the earth's foundation (also Psalm 102:25; Isaiah 40:22; Jeremiah 10:12 appears only as secondary 'by wisdom'). It is a distinct, widely repeated way the texts describe the making of the heavens and is not covered by the word, boundary or declare concepts. Only Job 38:4 (foundations) appears, and only as a secondary item.

missing.sub_theme: Let them praise the name of the LORD
missing.why: Psalm 148:5 is cited only for the command; the same psalm, with Psalm 96 and 98, calls the heavens, sea, creatures and trees to praise because they were created. A reader of this theme expects creation praising its Maker as well as declaring (Psalm 19), and the drafter's own concept 10 covers only declaring and testimony.

missing.sub_theme: In the beginning / before the mountains were born
missing.why: The texts speak of the beginning of the heavens and earth and of the Maker as before them; Genesis 1:1 and Psalm 90:2 may be on the front page already, in which case Proverbs 8:22–26 and Psalm 90:2 are the unplaced passages. Check against the front page before adding.
